tango_history.highest_value_visible_defect: K3 ROOT_DRIVE through K5 RELEASE_FORK flatten both arms into a near-horizontal crossbar, making the crucial body-earned release read like generic mannequin posing.
tango_history.concrete_correction: On the SAME 011 body, tuck the non-releasing guard arm downward and inward at K3-K6, keep the releasing arm on a higher forward diagonal, and increase torso lead so asymmetrical root/shoulder ownership is visible before release.

tango_history.inspection: Decoded representative decisive frames and final H.264 output. Asymmetric rear-hand load/torso coil now flows into a one-sided release; body recoil begins while the threat continues independently; delayed target contact occurs after recovery plant; post-contact body does not reverse toward the impact; release arm secondary lag and displaced settle repay debt.

Current worker deterministically rebuilt the 49-frame H.264 from the current-main abstract keys and timing and reproduced the declared media SHA byte-for-byte. Decoded dense release/recovery and decisive-key montages show asymmetric rear-load and torso coil, root-led release ownership, clear free-threat separation, body recoil beginning before delayed target contact, threat overshoot after contact, secondary release-arm lag, and a displaced non-idle settle. No mannequin symmetry, straight endpoint-only tween, farthest-reach body contact, reverse-interpolation recoil, or idle-reset recovery was observed.
